thread:
oliver: quick RFC follow-up on the fairness-scheduler adapter. main open Q: expose tenant weight as a soft hint or authoritative value? tradeoffs?

sarah: soft hint = safer rollout, less global coord, but can produce transient unfairness. easier on latency.

devon: authoritative needed for billing/SLA guarantees. requires global sync -> higher p99 and complexity.

julia: hybrid idea: edges accept weight_hint; central issues short-lived leases (authoritative) for tight SLAs. central reconciles longer windows and can issue corrections.

oliver: sounds reasonable. propose: admission token header contains lease_id, lease_expiry, weight_hint. edge uses hint; if authoritative lease present, it overrides.

devon: define mismatch semantics: if local vs central weight diverges by >X%, edge must enter conservative share mode until resync.

ops-bot: sim results: hint-only mode unfairness=2.1% p95; authoritative mode unfairness=0.3% but added ~12ms p99 latency.

sarah: rollout plan: default hint-mode globally, enterprise opt-in for authoritative leases. canary authoritative 3% for 48h.

julia: add console metrics: per-tenant weight, lease-staleness, local-fallback-count.

oliver: i'll write the RFC follow-up with header proto, lease TTL (30s), failure modes, and canary steps. tagging infra for canary slots.

ops-bot: reminder: include testing plan and SLO impact in RFC.
